requirements.requirement: Establish an IPsec tunnel between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) across the transit network
requirements.summary: VyOS site-to-site IPsec config (IKEv2, AES256/SHA256/MODP2048, PSK) applied via native CLI (cmd-72416e24be684171) and OPNsense Swanctl config applied via config.xml model edits (cmd-9086c1a420b54163). swanctl -l on node1 (cmd-e46783d259a04b93) and node2 (cmd-0422ffb075b84ec1) both show IKE_SA ESTABLISHED and CHILD_SA INSTALLED with matching local/remote selectors 10.10.1.0/24 <-> 10.10.2.0/24.

requirements.requirement: Both private networks (lan-a 10.10.1.0/24 and lan-b 10.10.2.0/24) are carried over the tunnel
requirements.summary: IPsec child SA selectors on both node1 and node2 explicitly list local 10.10.1.0/24 / remote 10.10.2.0/24 (and vice versa) — confirmed in swanctl output cmd-e46783d259a04b93 and cmd-0422ffb075b84ec1, matching the OPNsense config.xml child entry (cmd-6fa8d17420994504 grep) with local_ts/remote_ts set accordingly.

requirements.requirement: node3 and node4 reach each other by their private addresses
requirements.summary: Bidirectional ping from node3 (10.10.1.2) to node4 (10.10.2.2) and reverse succeeded with 0% loss after tunnel and firewall setup (cmd-993c8f607a0c40a9, cmd-ee93c63af73d4308), following earlier failures (cmd-d95e9e097d044773, cmd-c2e7d4ce1e334202) that were diagnosed and fixed by registering the enc0 pseudo-interface and adding firewall pass rules.

requirements.requirement: Traffic between node3 and node4 is encrypted in transit across the transit network
requirements.summary: tcpdump on node1's transit interface (eth1/eth2) during test pings shows only ESP packets crossing the transit network (10.10.3.1<->10.10.3.2), with plaintext ICMP visible only on the LAN-facing interface (eth2), not on the transit wire (cmd-b5ec8aaa23e04ad1, cmd-88a5782054bb4b65). This directly demonstrates encapsulation of the private-network traffic.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and validated on all four managed nodes
requirements.summary: For each node: pre-restart baseline captured (boot_id/kern.boottime plus healthy tunnel/ping state: cmd-c98310870b3c4049, cmd-adf16bcbdea94204, cmd-3e9392abc19b4045, cmd-7060dc2aa2ab4fb8), restart acknowledged (cmd-a8826abe83d34553, cmd-441a205d37cc4747, cmd-a1c33783c2434906, cmd-e845118a247b4e76), disconnection observed via timeouts/refused connections during the transition, then a different boot identity confirmed post-restart (cmd-9d1a01501d094a00 boot_id changed 2674ee60->6c5d5e63; cmd-09540ec0169d486c boottime changed 14:11:44->14:24:19; cmd-d39839efbebb413c boot_id changed 9094f607->a70b78e9; cmd-8cdb56b9e2a0488c boot_id changed a1dc8e25->bf0fab4d), and recovered state (interfaces, IPsec SA re-established, cross-tunnel ping) verified for each node (cmd-fff9434872e14acc, cmd-8c7a4ab4b2d54bf7, cmd-9db268189f0141ab, cmd-746ae12042704ad5, cmd-ff369e5ef7f74605, cmd-75eba0e7ec684804). The fixed lifecycle after-executor boot-identity snapshots corroborate all four boot ID/boottime changes independently.

overall_summary: The executor established a working IKEv2 site-to-site IPsec tunnel between VyOS (node1) and OPNsense (node2) carrying both lan-a and lan-b subnets, verified via swanctl status on both ends showing ESTABLISHED/INSTALLED SAs with correct traffic selectors. End-to-end reachability between node3 (10.10.1.2) and node4 (10.10.2.2) was directly demonstrated via successful bidirectional pings, and encryption-in-transit was directly confirmed via tcpdump showing only ESP traffic on the transit link while plaintext ICMP appeared only on the LAN side. The mandatory restart protocol was completed for all four nodes with clear before/restart/after boot-identity transitions and post-restart recovery of IPsec, routing, and cross-tunnel connectivity, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good: most state changes map directly to task requirements or corrective fixes for genuine configuration-discovery challenges (physical interface mapping ambiguity, OPNsense's enc0 registration requirement); minor leftover temp helper scripts on node2 are low-risk and not indicative of unsafe or destructive practice.
limitations: Traffic content (encrypted payload) was not decrypted/inspected to prove ESP genuinely carries ICMP for the exact test pings, but the correlation of timestamps between plaintext-on-LAN and ESP-on-transit captures during the same ping run is strong circumstantial evidence.

No SA byte/packet counters were observed incrementing beyond zero in the swanctl output shown, though this is a known artifact of when the snapshot was taken relative to traffic flow, not evidence of failure given the direct ping and tcpdump confirmation.
Small OPNsense helper scripts in /tmp (opn_add_ifaces.py, opn_ipsec.py, opn_fw.py) were not explicitly cleaned up by the executor; low risk but a minor tidiness gap.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the executor's chronological state-changing commands: nearly all mutations directly served the task (interface addressing, IPsec configuration, firewall rules, routes, restarts). A few sequences show iterative troubleshooting rather than clean unnecessary mutations: (1) on node1, an initial wrong interface-to-address mapping (cmd-4c85272547194cb0 assigning eth1=lan-a/eth2=transit) was empirically discovered wrong via failed pings and immediately corrected with a delete+re-set (cmd-d411b017acc04b93) — this is a corrective action fixing a genuine ambiguity (physical NIC order didn't match assumption), not a gratuitous experiment, and it left no residue since the final config is correct and persisted. (2) On node2, several attempts to reconfigure interfaces failed (configctl system configure 'Action not allowed', cmd-6a9effc08e27467d) before the working `configctl interface reconfigure opt1/opt2` command was found (cmd-e8b94dec4b4542fc) — these are read/attempt failures without evidence of a lasting harmful mutation. (3) Firewall rule reload attempts on node2 were repeated multiple times while debugging the enc0 interface registration gap (cmd-2fc6e173116744f0, cmd-8de1b0b1028f42e9, cmd-f8e56c6067e546af, cmd-5d6b0c97131942fc) — each is a legitimate step toward the necessary registration fix (pluginctl -i) and firewall reload, not abandoned residue. Temp files created via base64-decoded Python helper scripts (/tmp/opn_add_ifaces.py, /tmp/opn_ipsec.py, /tmp/opn_fw.py) remain on node2 per the after-executor temp-file diff, but these are small, low-risk config-application scripts consistent with the OPNsense config.xml editing approach — not high-risk residue, though ideally cleaned up. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening actions were observed; failed-services and package-health checks remain clean pre/post per lifecycle snapshots.
